simple.meaning: שָׁקַץ (shâqats) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to be filthy , i.e. (intensively) to loathe , pollute.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 7 times across Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Psalms, beginning at Leviticus 11:11. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.

firstOccurrence.englishText: and you shall detest them. You shall not eat of their meat, and you shall detest their carcasses.

majorEvents.label: Defilement
majorEvents.evidenceText: You shall not make yourselves abominable with any creeping thing that creeps. You shall not make yourselves unclean with them, that you should be defiled by them.

timeline.evidenceText: and you shall detest them. You shall not eat of their meat, and you shall detest their carcasses.
“ ‘You shall detest these among the birds; they shall not be eaten because they are an abomination: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
You shall not make yourselves abominable with any creeping thing that creeps. You shall not make yourselves unclean with them, that you should be defiled by them.

“ ‘You shall therefore make a distinction between the clean animal and the unclean, and between the unclean fowl and the clean. You shall not make yourselves abominable by animal, or by bird, or by anything with which the ground teems, which I have separated from you as unclean for you.
You shall not bring an abomination into your house and become a devoted thing like it. You shall utterly detest it. You shall utterly abhor it; for it is a devoted thing.
You shall not bring an abomination into your house and become a devoted thing like it. You shall utterly detest it. You shall utterly abhor it; for it is a devoted thing.
My praise of you comes in the great assembly.

definitions.full: H8262. shaqats [ שִׁקֵּץ ] verb Pi`el denominative detest, make detestable ; — Perfect 3masculine singular שִׁקַּץ Psa 22:25 ; Imperfect 2masculine plural תְּשַׁקְּצוּ Lev 11:13 +, etc.; Infinitive absolute שַׁקֵּץ Deut 7:26 ; — 1 detest , c. accusative of thing Deut 7:26 (Imperfect + Infinitive absolute; || תְּתַעֲבֶּנּוּ תַּעֵב ), Lev 11:11 , 13 (P); || בָּזָה Psa 22:25 2 make detestable , object נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם (= reflexive) Lev 11:43 (P), 20:25 (H).
